raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Integrates the Kimi-K3 merged MoE front from ROCm/aiter#5321.

Kimi-K3's MoE front applies three projections to the same `x[M, 7168]`:
shared gate/up `7168 -> 1536`, router logits `7168 -> 896`, and routed latent
`7168 -> 3584`. For the measured token counts this PR replaces them with one
BF16 GEMM into an FP32 `7168 -> 6016` accumulator followed by AITER's generic
SiTU/split epilogue. Routed experts remain on the existing modular AITER MXFP4
backend.

Unsupported configurations and token counts fall back to the native front.
There is no feature environment variable.

## Safety gate

The merged path is enabled only when all assumptions used by the optimized
implementation hold:

- gfx950;
- exact Kimi-K3 BF16 CUDA weight shapes and compatible devices;
- DP, EP, and PCP are all 1;
- sequence parallelism is disabled;
- the routed latent tail is shardable and has not already been reduced;
- modular routed experts are in use;
- activation is `SituAndMul(beta=4, linear_beta=25)`.

The runtime token gate intentionally matches the discrete set used for the
successful C1/C4 AgenticX measurements:

```text
1..16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 192,
512, 1024, 1536, 2048
```

This retains the prefill anchors that were enabled during those runs. Other
prefill remainders and larger shapes use the native path. Expanding prefill to a
continuous range is deferred to the separately measured AITER tuning follow-up.

## Resource lifecycle

hipBLASLt is initialized only when a selected tuned row actually dispatches to
hipBLASLt. Initialization is process-cached, and all Kimi-K3 MoE layers in one
worker share a single front workspace. Weight processing therefore does not
allocate one hipBLASLt workspace per layer or unnecessarily reduce the KV pool.

The native fallback calls the internal implementation directly so a fallback
from the custom-op boundary does not advance the MoE layer index twice.

## End-to-end results

MI355X, TP8, DSpark MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=3`). Both arms ran back to back
on one node with identical server and client arguments.

### 8K/1K fixed sequence length

| Concurrency | Decode M | Output throughput | Median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 130.1 -> 135.9 tok/s, **+4.43%** | 7.15 -> 6.83 ms, **-4.53%** |
| 4 | 16 | 369.9 -> 380.5 tok/s, **+2.87%** | 9.25 -> 8.97 ms, **-2.98%** |
| 8 | 32 | 582.8 -> 606.5 tok/s, **+4.07%** | 11.99 -> 11.31 ms, **-5.66%** |
| 16 | 64 | 799.8 -> 814.3 tok/s, **+1.82%** | 18.00 -> 17.65 ms, **-1.98%** |
| 32 | 128 | 1030.2 -> 1044.7 tok/s, **+1.41%** | 28.95 -> 28.55 ms, **-1.37%** |

### AgenticX trace replay, 3600 s per cell

The discrete gate above, including its prefill anchors, was enabled in these
runs.

| Metric | C1 | C4 |
|---|---|---|
| Output throughput | 84.77 -> 87.75 tok/s, **+3.52%** | 139.20 -> 146.61 tok/s, **+5.33%** |
| P90 TPOT | 8.92 -> 8.47 ms, **-5.03%** | 13.52 -> 13.36 ms, **-1.19%** |
| P90 interactivity | 112.1 -> 118.1 tok/s, **+5.29%** | 73.9 -> 74.8 tok/s, **+1.20%** |

## Accuracy

GSM8K, full 1319-question split, 5-shot greedy: baseline 0.9659 strict-match,
merged 0.9719. Of 24 discordant answers, 16 changed to correct and 8 to
incorrect (two-sided sign test p=0.15), consistent with run-to-run numerical
nondeterminism rather than an accuracy change.

## Validation

- Ruff format and lint on changed files: passed.
- Python syntax compilation on changed files: passed.
- DCO: passed.
- Existing Kimi-K3 runner tests from the prior revision: 59 passed.
- Existing companion AITER gfx950 tests from the prior revision: 17 passed.
- TP8 server startup and CUDA Graph capture from the prior revision: passed.
- MI355X C1/C4 AgenticX runs with the same discrete shape gate: passed.

Base AITER implementation: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5321

Future prefill tuning follow-up (not required by this revision):
https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5956

AI assistance was used to analyze benchmark results, update the implementation,
and prepare tests. The human submitter will review and owns the final change.



## Appendix: 2026-10-08 nightly AgenticX A/B rerun

A direct one-node MI355X Slurm A/B rerun reproduced the configuration from
[InferenceX run 36611233046, attempt 2](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36611233046/attempts/2).
The run did not use a CI runner. Both arms used the same node, image, models,
server arguments, and one-hour AgenticX profiling window per cell.

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100`
- Image digest: `sha256:1118faa948a879ae29a773d7f918b4d189c5b4b1d12198fd520dfe5279bdac7c`
- Baseline vLLM commit: `81198e97b`
- PR head represented by the overlay: `d1447951e396ea267216e2386da26fadf0ab44b3`
- C1: DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=7`
- C4: DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=5`

| Concurrency | Input throughput | Output throughput | Total throughput | P90 TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 13,270.88 -> 13,626.87 tok/s (**+2.68%**) | 109.41 -> 111.63 tok/s (**+2.03%**) | 13,380.29 -> 13,738.50 tok/s (**+2.68%**) | 5.84 -> 5.64 ms (**-3.42%**) |
| 4 | 23,230.21 -> 23,532.80 tok/s (**+1.30%**) | 173.33 -> 178.83 tok/s (**+3.17%**) | 23,403.54 -> 23,711.64 tok/s (**+1.32%**) | 7.93 -> 8.28 ms (**+4.41%**, worse) |

Both B cells completed and produced final JSON artifacts. B-C1 completed 221
requests with zero request errors. B-C4 completed 504 requests with zero request
errors; one in-flight request was cancelled at the final profiling grace cutoff.
CUDA Graph capture completed successfully for both cells.

Important compatibility caveat: the Kimi-K3 AITER tuning table in this nightly
contains hipBLASLt solution IDs generated for a different runtime. The current
runtime rejects the selected `443486` ID with `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`.
Therefore, the B arm included a local compatibility patch that keeps the single
merged `6016 x 7168` front GEMM but routes it through
`torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32)` instead of forcing the stale tuned ID.
These numbers validate the merged-front fallback on this nightly; they are not an
exact measurement of the unmodified PR's explicit tuned-solution path.

## AI model disclosure

- `GPT-5` (Codex runtime) diagnosed the nightly compatibility issue, orchestrated
  the direct Slurm A/B rerun, analyzed the result artifacts, and prepared this
  appended update. No delegated agents were used.
- The exact model/version used for AI assistance before this appended update could
  not be verified in this session.

nodes.body:
### GSM8K accuracy A/B

Adding the accuracy evidence this PR was missing. The numerical tests compare
the fused kernel against a `torch.mm` reference built from the same merged
weight, which is self-consistent and therefore blind to the one failure mode
specific to this change: the merged front slices its router logits out of a
`7168 -> 6016` accumulator where the native front runs a separate `7168 -> 896`
GEMM. Both are BF16 x BF16 -> FP32, but the wider shape picks a different
solution with a different accumulation order, and that rounding difference can
flip a borderline top-16 expert selection. Only an end-to-end score can see it.

Full 1319-question GSM8K test split, 5-shot, greedy. Both arms ran back to back
on one node from the same image, at `max_num_seqs=8` with
`num_speculative_tokens=3` and block rejection sampling, so a saturated decode
step submits 32 tokens and the merged front is the decode path for effectively
the whole run.

| Filter | Baseline | Merged |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict-match | 0.9659 | 0.9719 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9651 | 0.9712 |

Both arms answer the same questions, so the paired view is the informative one
rather than the unpaired +/- 0.005 binomial band: 1295 of 1319 answers agree, 16
flip to correct and 8 flip to incorrect, and an exact two-sided sign test on the
24 discordant pairs gives p = 0.15.

The merged front is indistinguishable from the native front on accuracy. The
+0.6 pp is run-to-run nondeterminism, not a claimed improvement.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @jiacao-amd.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

### GSM8K accuracy A/B

Adding the accuracy evidence this PR was missing. The numerical tests compare
the fused kernel against a `torch.mm` reference built from the same merged
weight, which is self-consistent and therefore blind to the one failure mode
specific to this change: the merged front slices its router logits out of a
`7168 -> 6016` accumulator where the native front runs a separate `7168 -> 896`
GEMM. Both are BF16 x BF16 -> FP32, but the wider shape picks a different
solution with a different accumulation order, and that rounding difference can
flip a borderline top-16 expert selection. Only an end-to-end score can see it.

Full 1319-question GSM8K test split, 5-shot, greedy. Both arms ran back to back
on one node from the same image, at `max_num_seqs=8` with
`num_speculative_tokens=3` and block rejection sampling, so a saturated decode
step submits 32 tokens and the merged front is the decode path for effectively
the whole run.

| Filter | Baseline | Merged |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict-match | 0.9659 | 0.9719 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9651 | 0.9712 |

Both arms answer the same questions, so the paired view is the informative one
rather than the unpaired +/- 0.005 binomial band: 1295 of 1319 answers agree, 16
flip to correct and 8 flip to incorrect, and an exact two-sided sign test on the
24 discordant pairs gives p = 0.15.

The merged front is indistinguishable from the native front on accuracy. The
+0.6 pp is run-to-run nondeterminism, not a claimed improvement.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @jiacao-amd.
